name: Relative Face Peeling Through a Convex Reduction
statement: Under the convex-reduction hypotheses, let $B$ be a nonempty coordinate-face intersection of the contraction $A$, contained in one projected section $X_t$, and put $T=B\times\{t\}$ and $C=D\cap B$. Then $X$ peels relatively to $T$ exactly when $A$ peels relatively to $B$ and $C$ is empty or corner-peelable. If $B$ is corner-peelable, the second condition follows automatically by pc-minor closure.
proof: Contracting a relative peeling of $X$ yields one of $A$ to $B$, while restricting its residual families to the opposite target face gives a peeling of $C$. Conversely, lift the relative order on $A$ by deleting each new-coordinate fibre. Convexity makes the corner-cube intersection with the reduction a face and its complement component-monochromatic, so each fibre deletion is one or two valid corner deletions. The remainder is $(B\times\{t\})\cup(C\times\{1-t\})$; a corner order of $C$ removes the opposite layer and leaves exactly $T$.
